hfaqs.a: No. Start with spoken Punjabi in Roman letters, and let Gurmukhi come second. Learners who speak first stay motivated far longer than learners who drill letters for a month before saying a word.
hfaqs.q: Must I learn Gurmukhi before speaking?

hfaqs.a: ਸਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਅਕਾਲ for respect, ਹਾਂ and ਨਹੀਂ, ਧੰਨਵਾਦ, ਮਾਫ਼ ਕਰਨਾ, ਠੀਕ ਹੈ, and ਮੈਂ — I. With those seven you can open any interaction in Punjab politely while your vocabulary grows underneath.
hfaqs.q: Which words should I learn in week one?

hfaqs.a: The three tones — high, low, level — on voiced aspirates, plus retroflexes. Ten minutes of daily listening retunes your ears within weeks; the pronunciation page walks you through each one.
hfaqs.q: What is the hardest part of Punjabi?

how.d: Short, plain-English explanations — no grammar walls, no jargon without a translation.
Each phrase speaks in a native Punjabi voice. Slow it to 0.2× and repeat until it sticks.
Every topic ends in practice: quiz yourself, then review the words until they stay.

topics.desc: ਸਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਅਕਾਲ and beyond — greet Punjab with warmth from your first word. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ਸਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਅਕਾਲ with folded hands — respectful everywhere, from Amritsar streets to village homes. Casual ਹੈਲੋ works with friends; ਸਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਅਕਾਲ never fails.
faqs.q: How do I say hello respectfully?

faqs.a: ਤੁਸੀਂ ਕਿਵੇਂ ਹੋ? (formal) or ਤੂੰ ਕਿਵੇਂ ਹੈਂ? (informal) — and answer ਮੈਂ ਠੀਕ ਹਾਂ, ਧੰਨਵਾਦ (I'm fine, thanks). Health-questions open Punjabi hearts.
faqs.q: How do I ask how someone is?

faqs.a: ਸ਼ੁਭ ਸਵੇਰ (good morning), ਸ਼ੁਭ ਦੁਪਹਿਰ (good afternoon), ਸ਼ੁਭ ਸ਼ਾਮ (good evening), ਸ਼ੁਭ ਰਾਤ (good night). Time-greetings show care; use them generously.

topics.lede: ਸਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਅਕਾਲ and beyond — greet Punjab with warmth from your first word.
topics.note: A note on ਸਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਅਕਾਲ. ਸਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਅਕਾਲ (sat sri akaal — truth is the timeless one) carries folded hands and genuine warmth — Punjab's universal key. Say it to drivers, CEOs and grandmothers alike; the returned smile is guaranteed. Respect first, everything else follows.
paras: Greetings open every door: ਸਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਅਕਾਲ (respectful hello), ਸਲਾਮ (warm hello), ਹੈਲੋ (casual hi). Fold your hands, say ਸਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਅਕਾਲ, and Punjab opens — dhabas, bazaars, homes. One word, infinite welcome.

Health-questions show you care: ਤੁਸੀਂ ਕਿਵੇਂ ਹੋ? (how are you, formal), ਮੈਂ ਠੀਕ ਹਾਂ (I'm fine), ਅਤੇ ਤੁਸੀਂ? (and you?). Punjabi small talk runs on genuine enquiry — ask properly, listen properly, belong quickly.

Time splits the day: ਸ਼ੁਭ ਸਵੇਰ (good morning), ਸ਼ੁਭ ਦੁਪਹਿਰ (good afternoon), ਸ਼ੁਭ ਸ਼ਾਮ (good evening), ਸ਼ੁਭ ਰਾਤ (good night). Morning greetings before noon, ਰਾਤ only at parting — timing your ਸ਼ੁਭ shows cultural fluency.

Partings promise return: ਰੱਬ ਰਾਖਾ (God protect you), ਫਿਰ ਮਿਲਾਂਗੇ (we'll meet again), ਆਪਣਾ ਖਿਆਲ ਰੱਖੋ (take care). Punjabis rarely say goodbye without a next meeting — ਫਿਰ ਮਿਲਾਂਗੇ assumes friendship continues. Say it warmly; mean it always.
topics.title: Saying hello the Punjabi way

topics.desc: ੳ ਅ ੲ to ਕ ਖ ਗ — Gurmukhi vowels, consonants and rows, made friendly. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Cousins — Gurmukhi shares Devanagari's order and logic with its own rounded shapes. Hindi readers learn Gurmukhi in days.
The first row: ੳ ਅ ੲ (vowel-bearers) then ਸ ਹ — the alphabet's name-order. Chant ੳ ਅ ੲ ਸ ਹ ਕ ਖ ਗ ਘ ਙ daily and letters stick.
Vowels first: ਅ ਆ ਇ ਈ ਉ ਊ ਏ ਐ ਓ ਔ — then ਕ ਖ ਗ ਘ ਚ ਛ ਜ ਝ. Sounds before shapes; reading follows speaking.

topics.lede: ੳ ਅ ੲ to ਕ ਖ ਗ — Gurmukhi vowels, consonants and rows, made friendly.

links.desc: Letters from zero, step by step.
links.label: Punjabi basics

topics.note: A note on ੳ ਅ ੲ. ੳ ਅ ੲ (uda, aada, aidi — the vowel-bearers) open the Gurmukhi alphabet — silent carriers that hold vowel signs. Chant them first in every practice; the alphabet's rhythm starts here.
paras: Vowels anchor everything: ਅ ਆ ਇ ਈ ਉ ਊ ਏ ਐ ਓ ਔ — ten pure sounds. Long-short pairs matter — ਇ vs ਈ changes meaning. Chant them in order daily; the mouth memorises what the ear repeats.

Consonants march in families: ਕ ਖ ਗ ਘ (throat), ਚ ਛ ਜ ਝ (palate), ਟ ਠ ਡ ਢ (roof), ਤ ਥ ਦ ਧ (teeth), ਪ ਫ ਬ ਭ (lips). Family by family, feel where each sound lives — Punjabi pronunciation is geography you can touch.
Special letters crown the set: ਯ ਰ ਲ ਵ ੜ ਸ਼ ਖ਼ ਗ਼ ਜ਼ ਫ਼ ਲ਼ — with ੜ (retroflex R) and dotted Persian loans. ਸਕੂਲ (school) and ਖ਼ਬਰ (news) show loans in action. Special letters, everyday words.
Rows grid it all: ਕ ਕਾ ਕਿ ਕੀ ਕੁ ਕੂ ਕੇ ਕੈ ਕੋ ਕੌ — each consonant through every vowel. One row mastered teaches all rows. Read rows aloud for a month; Gurmukhi becomes a friend for life.
topics.title: Punjabi alphabet

topics.desc: ਇੱਕ ਦੋ ਤਿੰਨ to ਸੌ — count, pay and bargain in Punjabi. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ਇੱਕ ਦੋ ਤਿੰਨ ਚਾਰ ਪੰਜ ਛੇ ਸੱਤ ਅੱਠ ਨੌਂ ਦਸ — chant to ten, then ਗਿਆਰਾਂ ਬਾਰਾਂ ਤੇਰਾਂ to twenty. Rhythm first, precision follows.
ਵੀਹ (20), ਤੀਹ (30), ਚਾਲੀ (40), ਪੰਜਾਹ (50) — then combine: ਇੱਕੀ (21), ਬੱਤੀ (32). Tens plus units, endlessly.
ਸੌ (100), ਹਜ਼ਾਰ (1000), ਲੱਖ (100,000). ਕਿੰਨੇ? (how many?) asks; numbers answer. Markets run on these three.

topics.lede: ਇੱਕ ਦੋ ਤਿੰਨ to ਸੌ — count, pay and bargain in Punjabi.
topics.note: A note on ਕਿੰਨੇ? ਕਿੰਨੇ? (kinne — how much / how many?) is Punjab's most useful question — ਕਿੰਨੇ ਰੁਪਏ? (how many rupees?), ਕਿੰਨੇ ਵੱਜੇ? (what time is it?). One word, every transaction. Ask ਕਿੰਨੇ fearlessly; numbers come to you.
paras: One to ten sings: ਇੱਕ ਦੋ ਤਿੰਨ ਚਾਰ ਪੰਜ ਛੇ ਸੱਤ ਅੱਠ ਨੌਂ ਦਸ — chant it walking, cooking, waiting. Punjabi numbers love rhythm; your tongue learns faster than your brain. Ten numbers, total freedom in every shop.
Teens climb steadily: ਗਿਆਰਾਂ ਬਾਰਾਂ ਤੇਰਾਂ ਚੌਦਾਂ ਪੰਦਰਾਂ ਸੋਲਾਂ ਸਤਾਰਾਂ ਅਠਾਰਾਂ ਉੱਨੀ ਵੀਹ — eleven to twenty. ਉੱਨੀ (19) and ਵੀਹ (20) open the tens; climb daily and teens become trivial.
Tens multiply power: ਵੀਹ ਤੀਹ ਚਾਲੀ ਪੰਜਾਹ ਸੱਠ ਸੱਤਰ ਅੱਸੀ ਨੱਬੇ ਸੌ — 20 to 100. Combine freely: ਇੱਕੀ (21), ਪੰਜੀ (25), ਸਤਾਈ (27) — the tongue-twisters that prove fluency.
Hundreds rule markets: ਸੌ (100), ਦੋ ਸੌ (200), ਹਜ਼ਾਰ (1000), ਲੱਖ (100,000). ਡੇਢ ਸੌ (150) and ਢਾਈ ਸੌ (250) charm shopkeepers — halves and quarters in pure Punjabi. Money talks; count it in Punjabi.
topics.title: Counting in Punjabi

topics.desc: ਮੈਂ, ਤੁਸੀਂ, ਹਾਂ, ਨਹੀਂ — hold your first real Punjabi conversations. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ਤੁਹਾਡਾ ਨਾਮ ਕੀ ਹੈ? (what's your name?) — answer ਮੇਰਾ ਨਾਮ ਰਾਹੁਲ ਹੈ (my name is Rahul). Names first, friendship follows.
faqs.q: How do I ask someone's name?

faqs.a: ਹਾਂ (yes), ਨਹੀਂ (no) — short, clear, universal. ਹਾਂ ਜੀ adds respect; ਨਾ is casual. Yes-no fluency first.
ਮੈਨੂੰ ਸਮਝ ਨਹੀਂ ਆਇਆ (I didn't understand) and ਹੌਲੀ ਬੋਲੋ (please speak slowly). Honesty tunes every speaker to your level.

topics.lede: ਮੈਂ, ਤੁਸੀਂ, ਹਾਂ, ਨਹੀਂ — hold your first real Punjabi conversations.

links.desc: Dialogues with audio, step by step.
links.label: Punjabi conversation lessons

topics.note: A note on ਮੈਨੂੰ. ਮੈਨੂੰ (mainun — to-me) is Punjabi's magic word — ਮੈਨੂੰ ਚਾਹੀਦਾ ਹੈ (I want), ਮੈਨੂੰ ਸਮਝ ਆਇਆ (I understood), ਮੈਨੂੰ ਪਤਾ ਹੈ (I know). Experiences flow TOWARD you in Punjabi; master ਮੈਨੂੰ and fifty sentences unlock.
paras: People anchor talk: ਮੈਂ (I), ਤੁਸੀਂ (you formal), ਉਹ (he/she), ਉਹ (they). ਮੈਂ ਪੰਜਾਬੀ ਸਿੱਖਦਾ ਹਾਂ (I'm learning Punjabi) — gender shows on verbs, proudly. Introduce yourself; conversations ignite.
Questions drive dialogue: ਕੀ? (what?), ਕਿੱਥੇ? (where?), ਕਦੋਂ? (when?), ਕਿਉਂ? (why?), ਕਿਵੇਂ? (how?). ਤੁਸੀਂ ਕਿੱਥੇ ਰਹਿੰਦੇ ਹੋ? (where do you live?) — one question word plus any verb equals conversation.
Politeness oils everything: ਕਿਰਪਾ ਕਰਕੇ (please) and ਮਾਫ਼ ਕਰਨਾ (sorry/excuse me). ਮਾਫ਼ ਕਰਨਾ, ਹੌਲੀ ਬੋਲੋ (sorry, speak slowly) — apologies plus requests, the learner's armour.

Repair keeps talk alive: ਮੈਨੂੰ ਸਮਝ ਨਹੀਂ ਆਇਆ (I didn't understand), ਫਿਰ ਦੱਸੋ (please say again), ਇਸਦਾ ਮਤਲਬ ਕੀ ਹੈ? (what does this mean?). Broken Punjabi beats silent perfection — stumble forward daily.
topics.title: Real Punjabi conversation

topics.desc: ਹੈ, ਜਾਣਾ, ਕਰਨਾ — the verbs that carry every Punjabi sentence. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ਮੈਂ ਹਾਂ (I am), ਤੂੰ ਹੈਂ, ਉਹ ਹੈ, ਅਸੀਂ ਹਾਂ, ਤੁਸੀਂ ਹੋ, ਉਹ ਹਨ. Being first, everything else after.
Present uses root + ਦਾ/ਦੀ/ਦੇ + ਹੈ: ਮੈਂ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ (I do, m), ਮੈਂ ਕਰਦੀ ਹਾਂ (f). Gender shows on every present verb.
faqs.q: How does the present tense work?

faqs.a: ਜਾਣਾ (to go), ਆਉਣਾ (to come), ਕਰਨਾ (to do), ਖਾਣਾ (to eat), ਬੋਲਣਾ (to speak). Five verbs, half of daily speech.

topics.lede: ਹੈ, ਜਾਣਾ, ਕਰਨਾ — the verbs that carry every Punjabi sentence.
topics.note: A note on ਹਾਂ/ਹੈ/ਹੋ. The ਹਾਂ family (haan/hai/ho) is Punjabi's heartbeat — ਮੈਂ ਹਾਂ (I am), ਉਹ ਹੈ (he/she is), ਤੁਸੀਂ ਹੋ (you are). Every present-tense sentence pulses with ਹ. Learn this family cold; the whole tense follows.
paras: Being grounds all: ਹਾਂ/ਹੈ (am/is/are) — ਮੈਂ ਹਾਂ (I am), ਅਸੀਂ ਹਾਂ (we are), ਤੁਸੀਂ ਹੋ (you are), ਉਹ ਹਨ (they are). ਹੈ anchors identity, place, state — ਮੈਂ ਇੱਥੇ ਹਾਂ (I'm here), ਮੈਂ ਠੀਕ ਹਾਂ (I'm fine). Be first.

Going and coming move life: ਜਾਣਾ (to go), ਆਉਣਾ (to come) — ਮੈਂ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ (I go), ਮੈਂ ਆਉਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ (I come). Direction verbs plus ਕਿੱਥੇ (where) navigate Punjab — ਮੈਂ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਸਰ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ (I'm going to Amritsar).
Doing and eating fill days: ਕਰਨਾ (to do), ਖਾਣਾ (to eat), ਪੀਣਾ (to drink) — ਮੈਂ ਕੰਮ ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ (I work), ਮੈਂ ਖਾਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ (I eat). Daily verbs, daily use; conjugate them in your sleep.
Speaking and knowing crown all: ਬੋਲਣਾ (to speak), ਪੜ੍ਹਨਾ (to read), ਲਿਖਣਾ (to write) — ਮੈਂ ਪੰਜਾਬੀ ਬੋਲਦਾ ਹਾਂ (I speak Punjabi). Say it now, imperfectly; say it daily until the mirror agrees.
topics.title: Punjabi verbs

topics.desc: ਪਾਣੀ, ਘਰ, ਕੰਮ, ਪਿਆਰ — the hundred words Punjabi daily life runs on. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Body, home, food, people: ਪਾਣੀ (water), ਘਰ (house), ਮਾਂ (mother), ਦੋਸਤ (friend). Concrete nouns first — point, name, own.
Adjectives agree with gender: ਚੰਗਾ (good-m), ਚੰਗੀ (f). Learn pairs together — agreement becomes music.
ਅੱਜ (today), ਕੱਲ੍ਹ (tomorrow), ਬੀਤਿਆ ਕੱਲ੍ਹ (yesterday), ਹੁਣ (now). Time words frame every plan — learn them this week.

topics.lede: ਪਾਣੀ, ਘਰ, ਕੰਮ, ਪਿਆਰ — the words Punjabi daily life runs on.

links.desc: Words in course order, with drills.
links.label: Punjabi vocabulary

topics.note: A note on ਵਧੀਆ. ਵਧੀਆ (vadheeyaa — nice/great) is Punjab's universal praise — ਵਧੀਆ ਹੈ (it's nice), ਬਹੁਤ ਵਧੀਆ (very nice). Food, films, friends' work — praise everything. Generous ਵਧੀਆ earns generous friendship.
paras: Survival nouns anchor reality: ਪਾਣੀ (water), ਖਾਣਾ (food), ਘਰ (house), ਰਸਤਾ (road). Point at each, say it aloud, use it today — ਪਾਣੀ ਚਾਹੀਦਾ ਹੈ (I want water). Concrete first, abstract later.
People words warm speech: ਬੰਦਾ (person), ਦੋਸਤ (friend), ਮਾਂ (mother), ਬੱਚਾ (child). ਮੇਰਾ ਦੋਸਤ (my friend) introduces proudly; ਮਾਂ calls home. People before things, always.
Describing words add colour: ਵੱਡਾ (big), ਛੋਟਾ (small), ਚੰਗਾ (good), ਨਵਾਂ (new). Adjectives dance with gender — ਵੱਡਾ ਭਰਾ (big brother), ਵੱਡੀ ਭੈਣ (big sister). Pair-learn each one.

Time and feeling complete the core: ਅੱਜ (today), ਪਿਆਰ (love), ਖੁਸ਼ੀ (joy), ਕੰਮ (work). ਅੱਜ ਬਹੁਤ ਕੰਮ ਹੈ (there's lots of work today) — then ਪਿਆਰ ਅਤੇ ਖੁਸ਼ੀ balance it. Words for living, not just talking.
topics.title: Core Punjabi vocabulary

topics.desc: ਸਰਸੋਂ ਦਾ ਸਾਗ to ਪਿੰਨੀਆਂ — order, eat and praise food in Punjabi. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ਖਾਣਾ (meal), ਨਾਸ਼ਤਾ (breakfast), ਚਾਹ (tea). ਮੈਨੂੰ ਭੁੱਖ ਲੱਗੀ ਹੈ (I'm hungry) opens every food conversation.
faqs.q: How do I talk about meals?

faqs.a: ਇਹ ਕੀ ਹੈ? (what is this?) and ਮੈਨੂੰ ਛੋਲੇ ਭਟੂਰੇ ਚਾਹੀਦੇ ਹਨ (I want chhole bhature). Point, ask, order — menus fear the curious.
ਮਸਾਲੇਦਾਰ (spicy), ਮਿੱਠਾ (sweet), ਲੂਣਾ (salty), ਖੱਟਾ (sour). ਘੱਟ ਮਸਾਲਾ (less spicy) saves sensitive tongues.

topics.lede: ਸਰਸੋਂ ਦਾ ਸਾਗ to ਪਿੰਨੀਆਂ — order, eat and praise food in Punjabi.
topics.note: A note on ਲੰਗਰ. ਲੰਗਰ (langar — free community kitchen) feeds millions daily at gurdwaras — ਰੋਟੀ, ਦਾਲ, ਪ੍ਰਸ਼ਾਦਾ for all, free, seated together. ਵਾਹਿਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਕਾ ਖਾਲਸਾ, ਵਾਹਿਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਕੀ ਫਤਿਹ. Food is seva; eating is prayer.
paras: Meals structure the day: ਨਾਸ਼ਤਾ (breakfast), ਖਾਣਾ (lunch/dinner), ਚਾਹ (tea). ਚਾਹ ਪੀਓਗੇ? (shall we have tea?) — Punjab runs on doodh-patti and conversation. Accept every cup; refuse nothing twice.

Ordering is easy bravery: ਮੈਨੂੰ ਇੱਕ ਚਾਹ ਚਾਹੀਦੀ ਹੈ (I want one tea), ਬਿੱਲ ਦੇ ਦਿਓ (please give the bill). ਇੱਕ ਪਲੇਟ ਛੋਲੇ ਭਟੂਰੇ ਦੇ ਦਿਓ (give one plate of chhole bhature) — order Punjab's soul in Punjabi. Dhabas reward attempts with extra butter.

Staples fill the thali: ਚਾਵਲ (rice), ਰੋਟੀ (flatbread), ਦਾਲ (lentils), ਸਬਜ਼ੀ (vegetables). ਸਬਜ਼ੀ ਕੀ ਹੈ? (what's the vegetable dish?) — ask daily, eat variously. Thali eating teaches vocabulary with every bite.

Tastes tune the tongue: ਮਸਾਲੇਦਾਰ (spicy), ਮਿੱਠਾ (sweet) — ਪਿੰਨੀਆਂ (sweet energy balls) crown winters. ਘੱਟ ਮਸਾਲਾ ਕਰ ਦਿਓ (make it less spicy) — then ਬਹੁਤ ਵਧੀਆ! (very nice!). Praise the cook; second helpings follow.
topics.title: Food phrases

topics.desc: Three tones, retroflex ੜ, bold rhythm — speak Punjabi like a native. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: The retroflex flap: tongue curls back, flaps forward — ਪੜ੍ਹਨਾ (to read), ਲੜਕਾ (boy). Practise flapping daily; Punjabi ੜ is bolder than Hindi ड़.
High, low and level pitch on words with ਘ ਝ ਢ ਧ ਭ — ਘਰ (house) falls, ਘੋੜਾ (horse) rises. Tones change meaning; ears learn them through songs.
Long-short pairs: ਇ/ਈ, ਉ/ਊ change words. Hold long vowels fully double — Punjabi ears measure length precisely.

topics.lede: Three tones, retroflex ੜ, bold rhythm — speak Punjabi like a native.
topics.note: A note on ਹੌਲੀ. ਹੌਲੀ (hauli — slowly) is the learner's best friend — ਹੌਲੀ ਬੋਲੋ (please speak slowly). Say it with a smile and every Punjabi speaker shifts to teacher-mode. Slow speech is kind speech; ask for it freely.
paras: The signature ੜ rules: ਪੜ੍ਹਨਾ (to read), ਲੜਕਾ (boy), ਕੁੜੀ (girl) — tongue back, flap forward. Minimal pairs drill it: ਪੜ੍ਹ (read!) vs ਪਰ (but). Master ੜ and Punjabis beam; skip it and they still understand, smiling.
Tones sing through speech: ਘਰ (house, falling), ਘੋੜਾ (horse, rising) — pitch shapes meaning. Don't fear tones; children absorb them from bhangra alone. Sing along; tones arrive.
Length carries meaning: ਇ vs ਈ, ਉ vs ਊ — short and long are different letters, different words. Double the long ones fully; clip the short ones crisp. Ears measure; mouths must comply.

Rhythm ties it together: ਹੌਲੀ (slowly) first, then natural speed; ਉੱਚੀ (loudly) for clarity, ਚੁੱਪ (quiet) for calm. ਉਚਾਰਨ (pronunciation) improves with echoing — shadow natives daily, record yourself weekly.
topics.title: Punjabi pronunciation

topics.desc: Two genders, postpositions, verb-final order — grammar without tears. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Masculine and feminine — nouns, adjectives AND verbs agree. ਚੰਗਾ/ਚੰਗੀ (good), ਜਾਂਦਾ/ਜਾਂਦੀ (go). Pairs everywhere; learn them as sets.
ਨੂੰ marks direction (ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਸਰ ਨੂੰ — to Amritsar), ਨੇ marks doers (ਰਾਮ ਨੇ ਕੀਤਾ — Ram did), ਨਾਲ means with. Postpositions follow nouns — learn each with ten examples.
Subject-Object-Verb: ਮੈਂ ਚਾਵਲ ਖਾਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ (I rice eat). Verb last, always. English order is the classic beginner error.

topics.lede: Two genders, postpositions, verb-final order — grammar without tears.
topics.note: A note on ਨੇ. ਨੇ (ne) marks the doer in past tense — ਰਾਮ ਨੇ ਕੀਤਾ (Ram did), ਮੈਂ ਖਾਧਾ (I ate). Ergative, elegant, everywhere in stories. Tiny suffix, enormous workload.
paras: Two genders shape everything: masculine (ਮੁੰਡਾ — boy), feminine (ਕੁੜੀ — girl). Adjectives pair — ਚੰਗਾ/ਚੰਗੀ — and verbs pair too. Gender is not decoration; it is Punjabi's skeleton.

Pronouns simplify persons: ਮੈਂ (I), ਤੂੰ (you-informal), ਤੁਸੀਂ (you-formal), ਉਹ (he-she/they), ਅਸੀਂ (we). ਅਸੀਂ vs ਆਪਾਂ (exclusive vs inclusive we) — Punjabi distinguishes; English doesn't. Choose your we wisely.
Postpositions replace prepositions: -ਨੂੰ (to), -ਨੇ (by/doer), -ਨਾਲ (with), -ਵਿੱਚ (in). ਘਰ ਨੂੰ ਜਾ (go home), ਚਮਚੇ ਨਾਲ ਖਾ (eat with a spoon). Suffixes after nouns — think backwards from English.

Verbs anchor sentences last: ਮੈਂ ਚਾਵਲ ਖਾਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ (I rice eat), ਉਹ ਸਕੂਲ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ (she to-school goes). Present (ਖਾਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ), past (ਖਾਧਾ), future (ਖਾਵਾਂਗਾ) — tense on verbs, time words framing. Verb-final: the one rule that never breaks.
topics.title: Punjabi grammar, plainly explained

topics.desc: Zero to first conversation — your first week of Punjabi, step by step. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ਸਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਅਕਾਲ, ਹਾਂ, ਨਹੀਂ, ਧੰਨਵਾਦ, ਮਾਫ਼ ਕਰਨਾ, ਠੀਕ ਹੈ, ਮੈਂ — seven words that open every door in Punjab. Speak them from day one.
faqs.q: What are my first seven words?

faqs.a: No — speak first in Roman letters, add Gurmukhi in week two. Speakers stay motivated; script-drillers quit. Talk today, read tomorrow.
Twenty focused minutes: five words, one dialogue, one song line. Daily beats marathon — streaks compound into fluency.

topics.lede: Zero to first conversation — your first week of Punjabi, step by step.
topics.note: A note on ਸ਼ੁਰੂਆਤ. ਸ਼ੁਰੂਆਤ (shuruaat — beginning) is the bravest word in Punjabi — ਅੱਜ ਤੋਂ ਸ਼ੁਰੂਆਤ (starting from today). Every fluent speaker once said their first broken ਸਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਅਕਾਲ. Begin badly; continue daily; arrive surely.
paras: Day one speaks: ਸਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਅਕਾਲ (hello), ਹਾਂ (yes), ਨਹੀਂ (no) — say them to mirrors, pets, shopkeepers. Pronunciation need not be perfect; attempts earn smiles and corrections. Speaking starts speaking; nothing else does.

Days two to four add survival: ਧੰਨਵਾਦ (thanks), ਮਾਫ਼ ਕਰਨਾ (sorry), ਪਾਣੀ (water), ਕਿੰਨੇ? (how much?). Four days, seven words, infinite transactions. Survival Punjabi fits in a pocket and works everywhere.

Days five to seven build sentences: ਮੈਂ ਅਧਿਆਪਕ ਹਾਂ (I am a teacher), ਮੈਨੂੰ ਚਾਹ ਚਾਹੀਦੀ ਹੈ (I want tea), ਤੁਸੀਂ ਕਿਵੇਂ ਹੋ? (how are you?). Frames plus words equal conversation — slots fill fast when frames stand ready.
Week two opens the script: ੳ ਅ ੲ, then ਕ ਖ ਗ ਘ — Gurmukhi through familiar words. Read what you already say; letters become friends, not walls. Speak-first learners read faster — motivation decodes.
topics.title: Punjabi for absolute beginners

topics.desc: ਮਾਂ, ਪਿਓ, ਦਾਦੀ, ਦਾਦਾ — family words that open Punjabi homes. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ਮਾਂ (mother), ਪਿਓ (father), ਭਰਾ (brother), ਭੈਣ (sister). Family first — Punjabis ask about yours within minutes.
ਚਾਚਾ (uncle), ਚਾਚੀ (aunt), ਦਾਦੀ (grandmother), ਦਾਦਾ (grandfather). Extended family, extended vocabulary.
ਮੇਰਾ ਪਰਿਵਾਰ ਵੱਡਾ ਹੈ (my family is big) — ਮੇਰੀ ਮਾਂ ਅਧਿਆਪਕ ਹੈ (my mother is a teacher). Describe yours; hearts open.
faqs.q: How do I describe my family?

topics.lede: ਮਾਂ, ਪਿਓ, ਦਾਦੀ, ਦਾਦਾ — family words that open Punjabi homes.
topics.note: A note on ਦਾਦੀ. ਦਾਦੀ (daadi — grandmother) rules Punjabi hearts — ਦਾਦੀ ਦੀਆਂ ਕਹਾਣੀਆਂ (grandmother's stories) raised generations. Learn ਦਾਦੀ and ਦਾਦਾ (grandfather); elders glow when learners speak family. Respect the roots; the tree welcomes you.
paras: Parents anchor all: ਮਾਂ (mother), ਪਿਓ (father) — ਮੇਰੀ ਮਾਂ (my mother), ਮੇਰਾ ਪਿਓ (my father). Punjabi children chant ਮਾਂ first; learners should too. Home begins here.
Siblings share childhood: ਭਰਾ (brother), ਭੈਣ (sister), ਵੱਡਾ ਭਰਾ (elder brother), ਵੱਡੀ ਭੈਣ (elder sister). ਵੱਡਾ marks respect for age — birth order lives in address. Call elders rightly; love follows.

Grandparents crown memory: ਦਾਦੀ (grandmother), ਦਾਦਾ (grandfather) — story-keepers, sweet-givers, wisdom-wells. ਮੇਰੀ ਦਾਦੀ ਸੋਹਣੀ ਕਹਾਣੀ ਸੁਣਾਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ (my grandmother tells lovely stories) — every Punjabi smiles. Honour them in speech.

The household gathers: ਪਰਿਵਾਰ (family), ਘਰ (home), ਵਿਆਹ (wedding), ਬੱਚਾ (child). ਮੇਰਾ ਪਰਿਵਾਰ ਵੱਡਾ ਹੈ (my family is big) — then listen; Punjabis narrate families with epic joy. Share yours; hear theirs.
topics.title: Family words

topics.desc: ਕਿੰਨੇ ਵੱਜੇ? ਸੋਮਵਾਰ to ਐਤਵਾਰ — time, days and dates in Punjabi. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ਕਿੰਨੇ ਵੱਜੇ? (how much has struck?) — answer ਪੰਜ ਵੱਜੇ (five o'clock). Time strikes in Punjabi; ask it everywhere.
faqs.q: How do I ask the time?

faqs.a: ਸੋਮਵਾਰ ਮੰਗਲਵਾਰ ਬੁੱਧਵਾਰ ਵੀਰਵਾਰ ਸ਼ੁੱਕਰਵਾਰ ਸ਼ਨੀਵਾਰ ਐਤਵਾਰ — chant the week; planet-days roll musically.
ਅੱਜ (today), ਕੱਲ੍ਹ (tomorrow), ਬੀਤਿਆ ਕੱਲ੍ਹ (yesterday), ਪਰਸੋਂ (day after/before). Four words frame every plan.

topics.lede: ਕਿੰਨੇ ਵੱਜੇ? ਸੋਮਵਾਰ to ਐਤਵਾਰ — time, days and dates.
topics.note: A note on ਵੱਜੇ. ਵੱਜੇ (vajje — has struck) makes time musical — ਕਿੰਨੇ ਵੱਜੇ? (how much has struck?), ਪੰਜ ਵੱਜੇ (five has struck). Clocks strike, bells ring, Punjabis ask poetically. Time doesn't pass; it chimes.
paras: Clock time strikes: ਕਿੰਨੇ ਵੱਜੇ? (what time?), ਇੱਕ ਵੱਜਿਆ (one o'clock), ਪੰਜ ਵੱਜੇ (five o'clock). ਸਾਢੇ ਪੰਜ (5:30), ਪੌਣੇ ਛੇ (5:45), ਸਵਾ ਛੇ (6:15) — halves and quarters sing. Ask time daily; numbers stick.
Day parts flow: ਸਵੇਰ (morning), ਦੁਪਹਿਰ (afternoon), ਸ਼ਾਮ (evening), ਰਾਤ (night). ਸਵੇਰੇ (in the morning), ਰਾਤ ਨੂੰ (at night) — suffixes time the day. Parts first, precision after.
Weeks cycle planet-wise: ਸੋਮਵਾਰ (Monday) through ਐਤਵਾਰ (Sunday) — Moon-day to Sun-day. ਅੱਜ ਸੋਮਵਾਰ ਹੈ (today is Monday) — date yourself daily. Weekdays rhythm life.
Dates frame plans: ਅੱਜ (today), ਕੱਲ੍ਹ (tomorrow), ਬੀਤਿਆ ਕੱਲ੍ਹ (yesterday), ਤਾਰੀਖ (date). ਕੱਲ੍ਹ ਮਿਲੀਏ? (shall we meet tomorrow?) — propose, confirm, arrive. Plans in Punjabi keep in Punjabi.
topics.title: Time and dates

topics.desc: ਟਿਕਟ, ਸਟੇਸ਼ਨ, ਕਿੱਥੇ? — travel Punjab by train, bus and word. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ਰੇਲਵੇ ਸਟੇਸ਼ਨ ਕਿੱਥੇ ਹੈ? (where is the railway station?) — swap in ਬੱਸ ਅੱਡਾ, ਹਵਾਈ ਅੱਡਾ. Where-questions navigate nations.
ਟਿਕਟ ਕਿੰਨੇ ਦੀ? (how much is the ticket?) and ਇੱਕ ਟਿਕਟ ਦੇ ਦਿਓ (give one ticket). Tickets first, journeys after.
ਸੱਜੇ (right), ਖੱਬੇ (left), ਸਿੱਧਾ (straight). ਸੱਜੇ ਮੁੜੋ (turn right) — direct and be directed.

topics.lede: ਟਿਕਟ, ਸਟੇਸ਼ਨ, ਕਿੱਥੇ? — travel Punjab by train, bus and word.
topics.note: A note on ਸਫ਼ਰ. ਸਫ਼ਰ (safar — journey) is Punjab's romance — ਰੇਲ ਸਫ਼ਰ (train journey) through mustard fields, winter fog on windows. ਸੁਖਾਲਾ ਸਫ਼ਰ (happy journey) blesses every traveller. Journey well; arrive storied.
paras: Stations start journeys: ਰੇਲਵੇ ਸਟੇਸ਼ਨ (railway station), ਬੱਸ ਅੱਡਾ (bus stand), ਹਵਾਈ ਅੱਡਾ (airport). ਸਟੇਸ਼ਨ ਕਿੱਥੇ ਹੈ? (where is the station?) — ask anyone; Punjabis direct travellers with pride.
Tickets buy passage: ਟਿਕਟ (ticket) — ਇੱਕ ਟਿਕਟ ਦੇ ਦਿਓ (give one ticket), ਟਿਕਟ ਕਿੰਨੇ ਦੀ? (how much?). ਗੱਡੀ ਕਦੋਂ ਆਵੇਗੀ? (when will the train come?) — ਗੱਡੀ means both train and car; context steers.
Directions decode cities: ਸੱਜੇ (right), ਖੱਬੇ (left), ਸਿੱਧਾ (straight), ਨੇੜੇ (near), ਦੂਰ (far). ਸਿੱਧਾ ਜਾਓ, ਫਿਰ ਸੱਜੇ (go straight, then right) — follow, arrive, thank.
Stays shelter nights: ਹੋਟਲ (hotel), ਕਮਰਾ (room), ਪਤਾ (address). ਕਮਰਾ ਕਿੰਨੇ ਦਾ? (how much for a room?) — bargain smiling, sleep soundly. ਸਫ਼ਰ ends in rest; rest remakes travellers.
topics.title: Travel phrases

topics.desc: ਕੀਮਤ, ਛੋਟ, ਰੰਗ — shop in Punjabi from first price to final deal. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ਇਹਦੀ ਕੀਮਤ ਕੀ ਹੈ? (what's the price of this?) — then ਬਸ ਕਿੰਨੇ? (just how much?) for everything else. Two questions, every shop in Punjab.
faqs.q: How do I ask the price?

faqs.a: ਬਹੁਤ ਮਹਿੰਗਾ ਹੈ (too costly) with a smile, then ਥੋੜ੍ਹਾ ਘੱਟ ਕਰੋ (reduce a little). Bargaining is friendly theatre — play your part warmly and the price moves.
Start with five: ਲਾਲ (red), ਨੀਲਾ (blue), ਹਰਾ (green), ਪੀਲਾ (yellow), ਚਿੱਟਾ (white). ਹੋਰ ਰੰਗ ਦਿਖਾਓ (show another colour) reveals the rest.

links.desc: Use these lines in real exchanges.

topics.note: A note on ਥੋੜ੍ਹਾ ਘੱਟ ਕਰੋ. ਥੋੜ੍ਹਾ ਘੱਟ ਕਰੋ (thodhaa ghatt karo — please reduce a little) is the magic sentence of Punjab's markets. Said smiling, it opens every negotiation; said with ਲਵਾਂਗਾ (I'll take it) right after, it closes most. Bargaining respects the dance, never the demand.
paras: Prices open every transaction: ਇਹਦੀ ਕੀਮਤ ਕੀ ਹੈ? (what's this one's price?), ਕਿੰਨੇ ਰੁਪਏ? (how many rupees?). Listen for the number, repeat it back — ਪੰਜਾਹ? (fifty?) — and you are already shopping in Punjabi.

Bargaining follows the friendly script: ਬਹੁਤ ਮਹਿੰਗਾ ਹੈ (too costly), ਛੋਟ ਦਿਓ (give a discount), ਥੋੜ੍ਹਾ ਘੱਟ ਕਰੋ (reduce a little). Start walking away slowly — ਚੰਗਾ, ਵੇਖਦਾ ਹਾਂ (okay, I'll look around) — and the real price often chases you down the street.

Sizes and colours refine the hunt: ਵੱਡਾ ਦਿਓ (give the big one), ਛੋਟਾ ਦਿਓ (give the small one), ਨਵਾਂ ਦਿਖਾਓ (show a new one), ਹੋਰ ਰੰਗ (another colour). Point, name the change, nod — Punjabi shopkeepers read gestures fluently and reward attempts instantly.

Colours close the sale: ਲਾਲ (red), ਨੀਲਾ (blue), ਹਰਾ (green), ਪੀਲਾ (yellow), ਚਿੱਟਾ (white), ਕਾਲਾ (black). ਲਾਲ ਵਧੀਆ ਲੱਗਦਾ ਹੈ (the red looks nice) — then ਲਵਾਂਗਾ (I'll take it). Deal done, in Punjabi, with a smile on both sides.
topics.title: Shopping and bargaining

topics.desc: ਮਦਦ, ਡਾਕਟਰ, ਹਸਪਤਾਲ — emergency Punjabi you hope to never need. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ਮੈਨੂੰ ਮਦਦ ਕਰੋ (please help me) — loud, clear, repeated. Add ਹਸਪਤਾਲ ਕਿੱਥੇ ਹੈ? (where is the hospital?) and Punjabi crowds mobilise instantly.
faqs.q: What is the one emergency sentence?

faqs.a: Point and say ਇੱਥੇ ਦਰਦ ਹੈ (it hurts here). Then ਮੈਨੂੰ ਚੰਗਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਲੱਗਦਾ (I feel unwell) and ਡਾਕਟਰ ਨੂੰ ਬੁਲਾਓ (call a doctor). Pain plus pointing crosses every language gap.
ਗੁਆਚ ਗਿਆ (it is lost) — ਪੈਸੇ ਗੁਆਚ ਗਏ (money lost), ਬੈਗ ਗੁਆਚ ਗਿਆ (bag lost). Then ਪੁਲਿਸ ਸਟੇਸ਼ਨ ਕਿੱਥੇ ਹੈ? (where is the police station?).
faqs.q: How do I report something lost?

topics.lede: ਮਦਦ, ਡਾਕਟਰ, ਹਸਪਤਾਲ — emergency Punjabi you hope to never need.
topics.note: A note on ਮਦਦ. ਮਦਦ (madad — help) is Punjabi's shortest lifeline — shout it and crowds come running. Punjab's bystander culture is famously kind: strangers will escort you to hospitals, translate for doctors, and refuse thanks. Ask loudly; receive gratefully.
paras: The core three save lives: ਮਦਦ (help), ਖ਼ਤਰਾ (danger), ਫੌਰੀ ਮਦਦ (urgent help). ਮੈਨੂੰ ਮਦਦ ਕਰੋ (please help me) — say it to anyone, anywhere. Punjabi crowds respond to distress calls faster than any app; your job is only to ask.
Medical words route the rescue: ਡਾਕਟਰ (doctor), ਹਸਪਤਾਲ (hospital), ਦਵਾਈ (medicine), ਮੈਡੀਕਲ (pharmacy). ਹਸਪਤਾਲ ਕਿੱਥੇ ਹੈ? (where is the hospital?) plus a taxi wave — in cities, help arrives in minutes.

Symptoms speak simply: ਇੱਥੇ ਦਰਦ ਹੈ (it hurts here, point!), ਮੈਨੂੰ ਚੰਗਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਲੱਗਦਾ (I feel unwell), ਸਿਰ ਦਰਦ (headache), ਬੁਖ਼ਾਰ (fever). Pain words plus pointing hands diagnose across every language barrier on earth.

Danger and loss close the kit: ਅੱਗ (fire), ਚੋਰ (thief), ਪੁਲਿਸ (police), ਗੁਆਚ ਗਿਆ (it's lost), ਦੂਤਘਰ (embassy). Memorise these cold — emergencies never wait for phrasebooks, and ten minutes of drilling buys total peace of mind.
topics.title: Emergency Punjabi

topics.desc: ਤੁਸੀਂ or ਤੂੰ? ਆਓ or ਆ? Respect levels, decoded with examples. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ਤੁਸੀਂ for every adult you don't know well — shopkeepers, officials, elders, strangers. ਤੂੰ waits for close friends, children and family. Wrong-side errors embarrass; learners are forgiven, but respect first is always safest.
Use the -ਓ form: ਆ becomes ਆਓ, ਜਾ becomes ਜਾਓ, ਦੱਸ becomes ਦੱਸੋ. One ending, instant politeness — the highest-value sound in Punjabi.
faqs.q: How do I make a command polite?

faqs.a: ਸਰਦਾਰ ਜੀ (sir) and ਭੈਣ ਜੀ for slightly-older strangers. ਸਰਦਾਰ ਜੀ, ਸਮਾਂ ਕੀ ਹੈ? (sir, what time is it?). Better than pointing and shouting in any language.

topics.lede: ਤੁਸੀਂ or ਤੂੰ? ਆਓ or ਆ? Respect levels, decoded.
topics.note: A note on -ਓ. The -ਓ ending (o) is Punjabi's respect rocket — ਆਓ (do come), ਵੇਖੋ (please see), ਦੱਸੋ (please tell). One sound that upgrades every request instantly. Stem-alone orders bark; -ਓ invites.
paras: Punjabi has two yous: ਤੁਸੀਂ (formal and plural — strangers, elders, officials) and ਤੂੰ (familiar — friends, children, family). English erased this distinction centuries ago; Punjabi keeps it razor-sharp. Every conversation opens with an invisible choice — make it consciously, and make it respectful.

Verbs mirror the split: ਆਓ (please come) versus ਆ (come!), ਦੱਸੋ (please say) versus ਦੱਸ (say!), ਜਾਓ (please go) versus ਜਾ (go!). The -ਓ ending is pure respect — same verb, different universe. Stems bark; -ਓ invites.

Giving and forgiving show the range: ਦਿਓ (please give) versus ਦੇ (give, familiar), ਮਾਫ਼ ਕਰੋ (please forgive) versus ਮਾਫ਼ ਕਰ (forgive, familiar). Beggars and kings both hear ਦਿਓ — politeness in Punjabi costs nothing and buys everything.

Strangers get titles: ਸਰਦਾਰ ਜੀ (sir), ਵੀਰ (brother), ਭੈਣ (sister). ਸਰਦਾਰ ਜੀ, ਮਦਦ ਕਰੋ (sir, please help) opens any door; barking orders at strangers closes them. Punjabi warmth is earned with two syllables of respect.
topics.title: Formal and informal Punjabi

topics.desc: Verb-first sentences, ਮੈਂ ਚਾਹੀਦਾ, ਨਹੀਂ vs ਨਾ — fix the classic errors. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: English order with Punjabi words: ਮੈਂ ਜਾ instead of ਮੈਂ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ, verb first, question words misplaced. Cure: every sentence ends with the verb — practise SOV until English order feels foreign.
faqs.q: What is the most common mistake?

faqs.a: Wanting flows toward people: ਮੈਨੂੰ ਚਾਹੀਦਾ ਹੈ (to-me it-is-wanted), never ਮੈਂ ਚਾਹੀਦਾ. One of Punjabi's deepest patterns — experiences come TO you — and beginners fight it for weeks.
ਨਹੀਂ denies verbs — ਪੈਸੇ ਨਹੀਂ ਹਨ (there's no money); ਨਾ answers no — ਨਾ, ਧੰਨਵਾਦ (no, thanks). Two no's, two jobs, zero overlap.

topics.lede: Verb-first sentences, ਮੈਂ ਚਾਹੀਦਾ, ਨਹੀਂ vs ਨਾ — fix them all.
topics.note: A note on ਗਲਤੀ. ਗਲਤੀ (galati — mistake) is the kindest word in this lesson — ਮੇਰੀ ਗਲਤੀ (my mistake) disarms every situation. Punjabis adore learners who err boldly and laugh warmly; the only true ਗਲਤੀ is silence.
paras: Mistake one: English word order. ਮੈਂ ਜਾ (I go — bare stem, wrong) instead of ਮੈਂ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ (I go — conjugated, right); verbs wandering mid-sentence instead of anchoring the end. Punjabi is verb-final, always — SOV is not a suggestion, it is the law.

Mistake two: ਮੈਂ ਚਾਹੀਦਾ (I want — wrong) instead of ਮੈਨੂੰ ਚਾਹੀਦਾ ਹੈ (to-me wanted — right). Punjabi wanting flows toward the wanter; English wanting fires from the wanter. Flip the arrow and dozens of sentences — ਮੈਨੂੰ ਸਮਝ ਆਇਆ, ਮੈਨੂੰ ਪਤਾ ਹੈ — unlock at once.

Mistake three: one-size no. ਨਹੀਂ denies verbs — ਪੈਸੇ ਨਹੀਂ ਹਨ (there's no money); ਨਾ refuses offers — ਚਾਹ ਨਾ (no tea for me). Beginners spray ਨਾ everywhere; natives smile and correct. Learn both no's, use each precisely.

Mistake four: rushing sounds — flat long vowels, missed tones, wrong gender endings. ਹੌਲੀ (slowly), ਸਹੀ (correctly), ਫਿਰ (again): the holy trinity of repair. ਕੋਸ਼ਿਸ਼ (effort) plus ਅਭਿਆਸ (practice) plus ਸਬਰ (patience) — and ਵਧਾਈਆਂ, mistakes become fluency.
topics.title: Mistakes every learner makes

topics.desc: Stop translating in your head — shadowing, thinking aloud and brave first speeches. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Shadow natives: play a Punjabi sentence, repeat it aloud half a second behind, matching rhythm and melody. Ten minutes daily rewires your mouth faster than any textbook.
faqs.q: What is the fastest speaking drill?

faqs.a: Yes — narrate your day in Punjabi: ਮੈਂ ਚਾਹ ਪੀਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ (I'm drinking tea), ਮੈਂ ਸਕੂਲ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ. Thinking aloud turns dead time into speaking practice.
faqs.q: Should I talk to myself in Punjabi?

faqs.a: Perfectionism. Punjabis reward every attempt and correct with love — ਬੋਲੋ, ਗਲਤੀ ਕੋਈ ਗੱਲ ਨਹੀਂ (speak, mistakes are fine). Fluency is corrected mistakes, stacked daily.

topics.note: A note on ਬੋਲੀਏ. ਬੋਲੀਏ (boliye — let's speak) is permission and invitation in one word — ਆਓ, ਪੰਜਾਬੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਬੋਲੀਏ (come, let's speak in Punjabi). Say it to every patient listener; doors, hearts and vocabularies open together.
paras: Speaking starts with shadowing: play a Punjabi line, echo it half a beat behind, copying music more than words. ਗੱਲਬਾਤ (conversation) is rhythm before grammar — shadow ten minutes daily and your mouth learns Punjabi's dance while your brain watches.

Questions and answers volley practice: ਸਵਾਲ (question) out, ਜਵਾਬ (answer) back. Ask yourself everything — ਇਹ ਕੀ ਹੈ? ਕਿੱਥੇ? ਕਿਉਂ? — and answer aloud. Self-volleys feel silly for a day, then feel like fluency arriving.

Opinions and stories stretch speeches: ਰਾਏ (opinion), ਸੱਚ (truth), ਕਹਾਣੀ (story). ਮੇਰੀ ਰਾਏ (in my opinion) forces full sentences; ਕਹਾਣੀ ਸੁਣਾਓ (tell a story) forces sequences. Opinions build sentences; stories build speakers.

Courage closes the circuit: ਹਿੰਮਤ (courage) speaks first and perfects later. ਗੀਤ (songs) loosen tongues, ਹਾਸਾ (laughter) dissolves fear, ਚੁੱਪ (pauses) are allowed. Speak badly today — ਭਾਸ਼ਣ (speech) improves only in motion.
topics.title: Speaking practice

topics.desc: Fast speech, films and radio — train your ears until Punjabi sounds slow. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Spoken Punjabi contracts: ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ melts toward ਜਾਂਦਾਂ, ਕਰਦਾ ਹਾਂ toward ਕਰਦਾਂ. Learn the full forms first, then meet the street forms — this page bridges both.
faqs.q: Why is spoken Punjabi so fast?

faqs.a: Children's films and songs first — clear speech, simple stories, endless repetition. Then ਰੇਡੀਓ dramas, then full ਫ਼ਿਲਮ (cinema). Difficulty ladders beat difficulty cliffs.
faqs.q: What should I listen to first?

faqs.a: Catch the question words — ਕੀ, ਕਿੱਥੇ, ਕੌਣ, ਕਦੋਂ — and the verb at the end. Questions plus verbs carry eighty percent of meaning; the rest is decoration.
faqs.q: How do I catch meaning in fast speech?

topics.note: A note on ਸਮਝ ਆਇਆ? ਸਮਝ ਆਇਆ? (samajh aayaa — do you understand?) is the kindest question in Punjabi — teachers, friends and auto drivers ask it constantly. Answer ਸਮਝ ਆਇਆ (understood) or ਥੋੜ੍ਹਾ ਥੋੜ੍ਹਾ (little by little); honesty tunes every speaker to your level.
paras: Listening begins with attention: ਧਿਆਨ (attention) — ਧਿਆਨ ਨਾਲ ਸੁਣੋ (listen carefully). Punjabi sentences save the verb for last, so ears must hold the whole sentence before meaning lands. Patience is a listening skill; practise holding, not guessing.

Street Punjabi contracts beautifully: ਜਾਂਦਾਂ, ਕਰਦਾਂ, ਬੋਲਦਾਂ — the melted present. Textbooks teach the full forms; ears must learn the melted ones. Listen for the verb-ghost at sentence end — the meaning hides there.

Media ladders the difficulty: ਗੀਤ (songs) first — slow, repetitive, emotional; ਖ਼ਬਰਾਂ (news) next — clear, formal, standard; ਰੇਡੀਓ (radio) drama third — fast, natural, fun; ਫ਼ਿਲਮ (films) last — slang, speed, glory. Climb rung by rung; never leap.

Active listening closes the loop: ਫਿਰ ਸੁਣੋ (listen again), ਆਵਾਜ਼ (sound) by ਆਵਾਜ਼. Replay each line three times — once for music, once for words, once for meaning. Three passes per line, ten lines per day: ears transform within a month.
topics.title: Understanding spoken Punjabi

topics.desc: Words to sentences to stories — reading Punjabi from first signs to full pages. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Signboards: ਦੁਕਾਨ (shop), ਸਟੇਸ਼ਨ (station), ਹੋਟਲ (restaurant) — big letters, daily repetition, instant rewards. Streets teach faster than textbooks.
Children's books — short ਵਾਕ (sentences), pictures for context, full conjuncts. Then comics, then ਅਖ਼ਬਾਰ headlines, then articles.
faqs.q: When am I ready for books?

faqs.a: Keep a ਸ਼ਬਦਕੋਸ਼ (dictionary) app open and mine unknown words — five per page, no more. Reading with a dictionary beats studying word lists: context glues memory.
faqs.q: How do I handle unknown words?

topics.lede: Words to sentences to stories — reading from first signs to full pages.
topics.note: A note on ਅਖ਼ਬਾਰ. Punjabi newspapers — ਅਜੀਤ, ਪੰਜਾਬੀ ਟ੍ਰਿਬਿਊਨ — use formal written Punjabi, nobler than street speech. Headlines first: big type, short lines, daily habit. One headline a day keeps illiteracy away.
paras: Reading starts with words: ਸ਼ਬਦ (word) by ਸ਼ਬਦ — ਪੜ੍ਹੋ (please read) signs, labels, names. Punjabi spelling mirrors speech, so sounding out works: see ਦੁਕਾਨ, say dukaan, know shop. Phonetic scripts reward beginners richly.

Sentences assemble next: ਵਾਕ (sentence) — subject, object, verb-last. Read SOV sentences end-first for meaning: find the verb, then ask who-did-what. Backwards parsing feels odd for a week, then automatic forever.

Paragraphs and articles follow: ਪੈਰਾ (paragraph), ਲੇਖ (article), ਕਵਿਤਾ (poem). Children's stories first — short, illustrated, kind — then ਰਸਾਲੇ (magazines), then ਸਾਹਿਤ (literature) itself. Punjabi's written heritage spans five centuries; start at the shallow end.

Dictionaries deepen everything: ਸ਼ਬਦਕੋਸ਼ (dictionary) — five new words per page, written down, reviewed nightly. Reading without recording entertains; reading with recording teaches. Mine every page; keep every gem.
topics.title: Reading Punjabi

topics.desc: Letters to lists to letters — writing Punjabi from first strokes to full pages. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Rounded strokes first: Gurmukhi letters curve gently — ੳ, ਅ, ਕ, ਮ. Trace big, shrink slowly; ਲਿਖਾਈ (handwriting) beautifies with mileage.
faqs.q: How do I start writing Punjabi?

faqs.a: ਸੂਚੀ (lists): shopping lists, word lists, daily plans. Lists forgive grammar, demand spelling, and get used — the perfect beginner writing.
ਚਿੱਠੀ (letters) to friends, ਨੋਟ (notes) to self, ਘਰ ਦਾ ਕੰਮ (homework) for courses. Real writing to real readers beats copied exercises every time.

topics.lede: Letters to lists to letters — writing from first strokes to full pages.
topics.note: A note on ਦਸਤਖ਼ਤ. Your ਦਸਤਖ਼ਤ (signature) in Gurmukhi is a milestone — practise it until it flows in one confident motion. Signing Punjabi-style on forms, cards and letters declares belonging more than any certificate.
paras: Writing starts with curves: Gurmukhi letters round and flow — ਲਿਖੋ (please write) circles and hooks before full letters. Trace ੳ ਅ ੲ ਕ ਖ big and slow; the hand learns shapes the eye already knows.
Tools matter little, mileage matters all: ਕਲਮ (pen), pencil, finger on steamed mirrors — Punjabi children trace in notebooks, slates and air. Write everywhere; medium is vanity, motion is learning.

Lists graduate the hand: ਸੂਚੀ (list) — ਨੋਟ (notes), ਪਤਾ (addresses), ਤਾਰੀਖ (dates). Copy your own ਨਾਮ (name) fifty times, then friends' names, then street names. Familiar words, fresh script: the fastest fluent hand.

Real writing arrives: ਚਿੱਠੀ (letters), ਅਰਜ਼ੀ (applications), ਇਮਤਿਹਾਨ (exams), ਘਰ ਦਾ ਕੰਮ (homework). Write a postcard to yourself in Punjabi — short, joyful, posted. First posted Punjabi is never forgotten.
topics.title: Writing Punjabi

topics.desc: Who does what, verb last — Punjabi sentences decoded with living examples. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Subject-Object-Verb: ਮੈਂ ਕਿਤਾਬ ਪੜ੍ਹਦਾ ਹਾਂ (I book read). Endings mark roles, so order flexes for emphasis — but verb-last is home.
Tense lives on the verb, with gender: ਪੜ੍ਹਦਾ/ਪੜ੍ਹਦੀ (read-present), ਪੜ੍ਹਿਆ (read-past), ਪੜ੍ਹਾਂਗਾ (will read). Time words — ਬੀਤਿਆ ਕੱਲ੍ਹ, ਅੱਜ, ਕੱਲ੍ਹ — frame it; the verb carries it.
Rise at the end: ਇਹ ਤੇਰੀ ਕਿਤਾਬ ਹੈ? (is this your book?). Question words — ਕੀ, ਕਿੱਥੇ, ਕੌਣ — sit where the answer would.

topics.lede: Who does what, verb last — sentences decoded with living examples.
topics.note: A note on ਮੀਂਹ ਪੈਂਦਾ ਹੈ. Punjabi weather does things: ਮੀਂਹ ਪੈਂਦਾ ਹੈ (rain falls), ਧੁੱਪ ਨਿਕਲੀ ਹੈ (sun is out), ਹਵਾ ਚੱਲਦੀ ਹੈ (wind blows). No empty it — Punjabi skies act. Weather sentences teach SOV with zero confusion: subject, then verb, done.
paras: Simple sentences stack three blocks: ਮੈਂ ਸਕੂਲ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹਾਂ (I — to-school — go), ਉਹ ਗੀਤ ਗਾਉਂਦੀ ਹੈ (she — song — sings), ਅਸੀਂ ਪੰਜਾਬੀ ਸਿੱਖਦੇ ਹਾਂ (we — Punjabi — study). Subject, object, verb — build a hundred of these and Punjabi skeleton is yours.

Animals make perfect practice: ਮੁੰਡਾ ਹੱਸਦਾ ਹੈ (the boy laughs), ਕੁੱਤਾ ਭੌਂਕਦਾ ਹੈ (the dog barks), ਬਿੱਲੀ ਸੌਂਦੀ ਹੈ (the cat sleeps). Short subjects, vivid verbs, zero ambiguity — describe every creature you meet and SOV becomes reflex.

Time flexes the frame: ਮੈਂ ਕੱਲ੍ਹ ਆਵਾਂਗਾ (I'll come tomorrow), ਬੀਤਿਆ ਕੱਲ੍ਹ ਮੀਂਹ ਪਿਆ (it rained yesterday). Time words float — front for emphasis, middle for flow — while the verb holds the end. Tense plus time word: past, present, future, mastered.

Identity and questions close the set: ਇਹ ਮੇਰਾ ਘਰ ਹੈ (this is my house), ਇਹ ਤੇਰੀ ਕਿਤਾਬ ਹੈ? (is this your book?), ਸਭ ਠੀਕ ਹੈ (all is well). Equate with ਇਹ/ਉਹ, question with rising tone, reassure with ਸਭ ਠੀਕ ਹੈ — sentences for every situation.
topics.title: Punjabi sentence structure

topics.desc: Rahul becomes ਰਾਹੁਲ — spell, write and own your name in Gurmukhi. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Sound it out in Gurmukhi letters: Rahul → ਰਾਹੁਲ, Priya → ਪ੍ਰਿਯਾ, John → ਜਾਨ. Punjabi spells by ear — say your name slowly, catch each sound, write each letter.
faqs.q: How do I write my name in Punjabi?

faqs.a: Dotted letters — ਖ਼ (kha), ਗ਼ (gha), ਜ਼ (za), ਫ਼ (fa) — handle foreign sounds. ਫ਼ੋਨ (phone), ਖ਼ਬਰ (news) — spotted letters for imported sounds, fully Punjabi now.
ਪਹਿਲਾ ਅੱਖਰ (first letter) starts it, ਆਖ਼ਰੀ ਅੱਖਰ (last letter) ends it. Introduce with ਮੇਰਾ ਨਾਮ (my name is), then write it — introductions stick twice as well written.
faqs.q: How do I introduce my name?

topics.lede: Rahul becomes ਰਾਹੁਲ — spell, write and own your name in Gurmukhi.
topics.note: A note on ਰਾਹੁਲ. Foreign names glide in Gurmukhi — Rahul appears as ਰਾਹੁਲ, sometimes ਰਾਹੂਲ with a longer vowel. All are read Rahul; none is wrong. Punjabi welcomes foreign names with flexible spelling — pick the shape you love and own it.
paras: Names transliterate by ear: break yours into sounds, match each to Gurmukhi letters — ਰਵੀ (Ravi), ਲਕਸ਼ਮੀ (Lakshmi), ਕਿਰਨ (Kiran) show the pattern. Say it slow, write it true — ਸਪੈਲਿੰਗ (spelling) by sound, not by English letters.

Foreign sounds borrow dotted letters: ਖ਼ for khabar-sounds (ਖ਼ਬਰ), ਫ਼ for phone (ਫ਼ੋਨ), ਜ਼ for azure (ਅਜ਼ਰ). These spotted letters are Punjabi citizens now — use them proudly for every imported sound.

Introductions pair speech and script: ਜਾਣ-ਪਛਾਣ (introduction) — ਮੇਰਾ ਨਾਮ (my name is), spoken, then written. ਨਾਮ ਵਾਲੇ ਬੋਰਡ (name boards) on doors and desks teach daily — read every board, collect every name.

Nicknames warm everything: ਪਿਆਰ ਦਾ ਨਾਮ (nickname) — ਬੱਬੂ (dear child), ਸੋਨਾ (golden one), ਗੁੱਡੀ (little doll). Punjabi shortens with love: Ravi becomes ਰਵੀ, Simran becomes ਸਿੰਮੀ. Earn a Punjabi nickname and you have arrived.
topics.title: Write your name in Punjabi

topics.desc: ਬੱਲੇ ਬੱਲੇ, ਚੱਕ ਦੇ, ਇੱਕ ਨੰਬਰ — street Punjabi that films, friends and fun run on. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ਬੱਲੇ ਬੱਲੇ (hooray) and ਇੱਕ ਨੰਬਰ (number one) — positive, universal, safe. Sprinkle them on food, films and friends; instant insider status.
ਵੀਰ (bro) and ਭਰਾਵਾ (brother mine) — for friends only, never elders or strangers. Friendship slang misused offends; rightly used, it bonds instantly.
Hanging out, passing time joyfully — ਕੀ ਚੱਲਦਾ ਹੈ? — ਕੁਝ ਨਹੀਂ, ਟਾਈਮਪਾਸ (what's up? — nothing, timepass). The most Punjabi answer in existence: relaxed joy, declared proudly.

topics.lede: ਬੱਲੇ ਬੱਲੇ, ਚੱਕ ਦੇ, ਇੱਕ ਨੰਬਰ — street Punjabi that fun runs on.
topics.note: A note on ਚੱਕ ਦੇ ਫੱਟੇ. ਚੱਕ ਦੇ ਫੱਟੇ (chak de fatte — lift the planks, go for it!) is Punjab's battle-cry — sports, exams, life. Shout it with friends; charge at everything. Three words, total fearlessness.
paras: Praise slang opens doors: ਬੱਲੇ ਬੱਲੇ (hooray), ਇੱਕ ਨੰਬਰ (number one), ਚੱਕ ਦੇ (go for it), ਫ਼ਸਟ ਕਲਾਸ (first class), ਕੈਂਟ (solid). Food, films, friends' outfits — praise everything loudly. Punjabis praise generously; learners should too.

Friendship words bond crews: ਵੀਰ (bro), ਭਰਾਵਾ (brother mine), ਯਾਰ (buddy) — friends-only, always warm. ਵੀਰੇ, ਆ ਨਾ (come on bro) starts a thousand conversations daily. Never aim them upward at elders; sideways at friends, fire freely.

Reaction words colour stories: ਹਾਏ ਓ ਰੱਬਾ (oh my God!), ਵਾਹ ਜੀ ਵਾਹ (wow!), ਗੱਪਾਂ ਨਾ ਮਾਰ (stop making things up!). Punjabi storytelling runs on reactions — gasp, laugh, disbelieve theatrically. Flat faces kill stories; big reactions feed them.

Playful edges season everything: ਚੱਲ ਨਿਕਲ (get lost — playful among friends, rude otherwise), ਛੀ (mild disgust), ਟਾਈਮਪਾਸ (chilling). Learn the edges, respect the edges: slang's power is knowing exactly where fun ends.
topics.title: Punjabi slang

topics.desc: Toys, moons, stars and good-child gold — Punjabi for little learners, big joy. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Songs and ਕਹਾਣੀ (stories) — ਗੀਤ with actions, tales with voices. Children absorb Punjabi through music and play long before grammar.
faqs.q: How do kids learn Punjabi best?

faqs.a: ਚੰਗਾ ਬੱਚਾ (good child) — praise every attempt loudly. Punjabi parenting runs on encouragement; learners of all ages bloom under it.
faqs.q: How do I praise a child?

faqs.a: ਖੇਡ (games): name objects — ਗੇਂਦ! ਖਿਡੌਣਾ! — count steps, sing counts. Play first, words hitchhike.

topics.lede: Toys, moons, stars and gold stars — Punjabi for little learners, big joy.
topics.note: A note on ਬੱਬੂ. ਬੱਬੂ (babbu — baby/darling) melts every Punjabi heart — ਮੇਰਾ ਬੱਬੂ (my darling) for children, pets and beloveds. Terms of endearment are Punjabi's mother tongue; every child swims in them.
paras: Little learners start with love: ਬੱਚੇ (children), ਬੱਬੂ (baby), ਸੋਨਾ (golden one), ਚੰਗਾ ਬੱਚਾ (good child). Punjabi childhood floats on affection-words — call every child ਬੱਬੂ and watch faces light like ਦੀਵਾਲੀ.
Play teaches fastest: ਖੇਡ (play), ਖਿਡੌਣਾ (toy), ਗੇਂਦ (ball) — ਖੇਡੀਏ (let's play)! Count throws, name colours, chase and giggle. Play first; Punjabi hitchhikes on joy.
School words structure days: ਸਕੂਲ (school), ਅਧਿਆਪਕ (teacher), ਪਾਠ (lesson), ਘਰ ਦਾ ਕੰਮ (homework). ਸਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਅਕਾਲ ਸਰ (hello sir) opens every school day — respect and learning, hand in hand.

Sky words spark wonder: ਸੂਰਜ (sun), ਚੰਨ (moon), ਤਾਰਾ (star) — ਚੰਨ ਵੇਖ (look at the moon)! Night-sky Punjabi, whispered on terraces, becomes lifelong memory. Teach the sky; the child keeps the language.
topics.title: Punjabi for kids

topics.desc: Meetings, customers, contracts — professional Punjabi for offices and business. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ਸਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਅਕਾਲ, ਮੈਂ (hello, I'm) — then ਤੁਹਾਨੂੰ ਮਿਲਕੇ ਖੁਸ਼ੀ ਹੋਈ (pleased to meet you). Business Punjabi opens formal and warms slowly.
faqs.q: How do I introduce myself at work?

faqs.a: ਮੀਟਿੰਗ ਕਦੋਂ ਹੈ? (when is the meeting?) and ਮੀਟਿੰਗ ਕਿੱਥੇ ਹੈ? (where?). Meetings run Punjabi offices — never miss one for language reasons.
faqs.q: How do I ask about meetings?

faqs.a: ਈਮੇਲ ਭੇਜਾਂਗਾ (I'll send an email) and ਫ਼ੋਨ ਤੇ ਗੱਲ ਕਰੀਏ (let's talk on the phone). Digital Punjabi borrows freely — clarity beats purity in business.

topics.lede: Meetings, customers, contracts — professional Punjabi for offices.
topics.note: A note on ਗਾਹਕ. ਗਾਹਕ (gaahak — customer) rules Punjabi business — ਗਾਹਕ ਹੀ ਰਾਜਾ (the customer is king). Master it syllable by syllable; clients notice the effort and reward it.
paras: Workplaces run on roles: ਨੌਕਰੀ (job), ਦਫ਼ਤਰ (office), ਬੌਸ (boss), ਗਾਹਕ (customer), ਸਹਿਕਰਮੀ (colleague). ਮੇਰੀ ਨੌਕਰੀ (my job is) introduces your profession; ਦਫ਼ਤਰ ਕਿੱਥੇ ਹੈ? finds any office. Roles first, tasks second.

Meetings move business: ਮੀਟਿੰਗ (meeting), ਇਕਰਾਰ (contract/deal), ਦਸਤਖ਼ਤ (signature). ਮੀਟਿੰਗ ਕੱਲ੍ਹ ਸਵੇਰੇ (meeting tomorrow morning) — confirm with ਠੀਕ ਹੈ, ਆਵਾਂਗਾ (okay, I'll come). Punjabi meetings open with ਸਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਅਕਾਲ and close with ਧੰਨਵਾਦ.

Money talks plainly: ਮੁਨਾਫ਼ਾ (profit), ਘਾਟਾ (loss), ਤਨਖ਼ਾਹ (salary), ਛੁੱਟੀ (leave). ਤਨਖ਼ਾਹ ਕਦੋਂ ਮਿਲਦੀ ਹੈ? (when is payday?) — asked smiling, everywhere. Business Punjabi respects directness wrapped in politeness.
Digital tools connect all: ਈਮੇਲ (email), ਫ਼ੋਨ (phone), ਸੁਨੇਹਾ (message). ਈਮੇਲ ਵੇਖੋ (please check email) — then ਸਫ਼ਲਤਾ (success) follows effort. Professional Punjabi: formal words, warm heart.
topics.title: Punjabi for work and business

topics.desc: Guru Granth Sahib, gurdwaras, Vaisakhi — reclaim the Punjabi your family carried. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Start with sounds you half-know: family words, food names, festival greetings. Heritage ears remember more than they admit — recognition unlocks fast, then production follows.
faqs.q: I understand but can't speak — help?

faqs.a: ਜਪੁਜੀ ਸਾਹਿਬ (Japji Sahib) — Guru Nanak's dawn prayer, the Sikh soul-song. Learn one pauri by heart; Punjabis of every age will beam.
faqs.q: What is the one classic to know?

faqs.a: ਵਿਸਾਖੀ ਦੀਆਂ ਵਧਾਈਆਂ (Vaisakhi greetings) and ਦੀਵਾਲੀ ਦੀਆਂ ਵਧਾਈਆਂ (Diwali greetings) — festivals are heritage made annual. Greet first, belong instantly.

topics.lede: Guru Granth Sahib, gurdwaras, Vaisakhi — reclaim the Punjabi your family carried.
topics.note: A note on ਮਾਂ-ਬੋਲੀ. ਮਾਂ-ਬੋਲੀ (maan-boli — mother tongue) is Punjabi's most emotional word — language as mother. ਮੇਰੀ ਮਾਂ-ਬੋਲੀ ਪੰਜਾਬੀ (my mother tongue is Punjabi) is identity declared. Heritage learners don't study Punjabi; they come home to it.
paras: Heritage starts with recognition: ਵਿਰਸਾ (heritage), ਵਡੇਰੇ (ancestors), ਮਾਂ-ਬੋਲੀ (mother tongue), ਸੱਭਿਆਚਾਰ (culture). Words you heard at knees and kitchens — say them now deliberately. Passive memory converts to active speech within weeks of trying.

Gurdwaras anchor memory: ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰਾ (gurdwara), ਹਰਿਮੰਦਰ ਸਾਹਿਬ (Golden Temple), ਲੰਗਰ (community kitchen). Every heritage family carries gurdwara-Punjabi — kirtan-lines, ardaas-words, seva-spirit. Visit a ਗੁਰਦੁਆਰਾ with learning ears; childhood vocabulary resurfaces like monsoon wells.

Festivals calendar the year: ਵਿਸਾਖੀ (harvest, April), ਦੀਵਾਲੀ (October-November), ਲੋਹੜੀ (winter bonfire, January). Festival kitchens teach fastest — grind, stir, taste, name everything. Heritage you can eat stays learned.

Classics crown the journey: ਬਾਬਾ ਫ਼ਰੀਦ (Baba Farid's sloks), ਵਾਰਿਸ ਸ਼ਾਹ (Waris Shah's Heer), ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਸਰ to ਲੁਧਿਆਣਾ — ਪੰਜਾਬ entire. One verse memorised outweighs ten lessons completed; heritage learners carry literature, not just language.
topics.title: Punjabi for heritage learners

topics.desc: Weeks to chat, months to flow, a year to shine — honest timelines, faster methods. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Survival in 2–4 weeks (greetings, numbers, food), conversation in 3–6 months, comfort in a year — at 20 minutes daily. Consistency beats intensity every time.
faqs.q: How long to hold a conversation?

faqs.a: Tones, ੜ, two-gender verbs — ਜਾਂਦਾ, ਜਾਂਦੀ. Each surrenders to weeks of drilling — this track attacks every one directly.
Daily contact plus weekly speaking: ਰੋਜ਼ ਅਭਿਆਸ (practise daily), ਹਫ਼ਤੇ ਬੋਲੋ (speak weekly). Apps maintain; conversations advance.

topics.lede: Weeks to chat, months to flow, a year to shine — honest timelines.
topics.note: A note on ਰੋਜ਼. ਰੋਜ਼ (roz — daily, every day) is the whole secret — ਰੋਜ਼ ਥੋੜ੍ਹਾ (a little every day) beats weekend marathons completely. Streaks compound; Punjabi rewards the faithful, not the frantic.
paras: Levels ladder clearly: ਸ਼ੁਰੂਆਤੀ ਪੱਧਰ (beginner — weeks 1–8: survival phrases, core sounds), ਵਿਚਕਾਰਲਾ (intermediate — months 3–8: conversations, tenses, reading), ਉੱਚਾ (advanced — month 9+: films, debates, literature). Each ਪੱਧਰ (level) feels impossible until suddenly it doesn't.

Habits beat hours: ਰੋਜ਼ (daily) contact, ਆਦਤ (habit) over heroics. Fifteen minutes of ਰੋਜ਼ practice — five words, one dialogue, one song line — compounds to fluency while motivation merely visits. Streaks are sacred; protect yours.

Goals steer progress: ਟੀਚਾ (goal) — ਸ਼ੁਰੂਆਤ (start) with survival, ਤਰੱਕੀ (progress) monthly measured. This month: order food. Next: small talk. Then: phone calls. Concrete ਟੀਚਾ, celebrated loudly — ਰਵਾਨਗੀ (fluency) is a trail of kept promises.

Mastery crowns patience: ਮੁਹਾਰਤ (mastery), ਪੱਕਾ ਇਰਾਦਾ (determination), ਆਤਮ-ਵਿਸ਼ਵਾਸ (confidence). A year of faithful days buys comfortable conversation; two buys belonging. Punjabi has waited five centuries — it will wait for you, and reward you richly.
topics.title: How long does Punjabi take?

topics.desc: Indo-Aryan roots, Sanskrit elders, Hindi neighbours — Punjabi's place in India's language family. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Close cousins — Punjabi and Hindi are both Indo-Aryan, sharing thousands of words. Same grandparents, different scripts.
ਹਿੰਦੀ for daily overlap, ਉਰਦੂ across the border, then ਸੰਸਕ੍ਰਿਤ above all. The punjabi-vs-hindi page maps the closest pair.
faqs.q: Which language is closest to Punjabi?

faqs.a: Two millennia of poetry, prayer and scholarship — ਸੰਸਕ੍ਰਿਤ words fill formal Punjabi while grammar stays Prakrit-born. Sanskrit lends vocabulary; Punjabi keeps its soul.
faqs.q: Why so much Sanskrit in Punjabi?

topics.lede: Indo-Aryan roots, Sanskrit elders, Hindi neighbours — Punjabi's family place.
topics.note: A note on ਪੰਜਾਬੀਅਤ. ਪੰਜਾਬੀਅਤ (Punjabi spirit) runs deep and joyful — language, food, music, courage. From Bhangra to global diaspora, Punjabi pride travels worldwide; learners inherit the celebration.
paras: Punjabi anchors northern India: ਹਿੰਦੀ (Hindi), ਉਰਦੂ (Urdu), ਬੰਗਾਲੀ (Bengali) — cousins, not strangers. Shared Sanskrit roots, shared ancient words, proud separate literatures. Learn Punjabi and Hindi signboards start whispering.
The south speaks Dravidian: ਤਮਿਲ (Tamil), ਤੇਲਗੂ (Telugu), ਕੰਨੜ (Kannada), ਮਲਿਆਲਮ (Malayalam) — different family, shared nation: ਭਾਰਤ (India) holds both, and ਅਨੁਵਾਦ (translation) bridges all.

Sanskrit threads everything: ਸੰਸਕ੍ਰਿਤ lent Punjabi thousands of formal words — ਤਤਸਮ vocabulary crowns speeches and scriptures. Daily speech mixes happily. Both registers are real Punjabi; learners need both.

Unity crowns diversity: ਏਕਤਾ (unity) — 22 official languages, hundreds of mother tongues, one conversation. Punjabis learn Hindi for Delhi, English for globe, Punjabi for soul. Every Indian language you meet makes your Punjabi richer.
topics.title: Punjabi among Indian languages

topics.desc: Cousin languages, sister scripts — shared words, split sounds, mutual love. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Largely yes for simple speech — ਘਰ, ਪਾਣੀ, ਨਾਮ, ਨਹੀਂ/नहीं are near-identical. Speed and slang divide them; patience reunites them.
Punjabi kept tones and bold retroflexes; Hindi softened both. Cousins with different habits — precisely the words learners say most.
faqs.q: Why do they sound similar yet different?

faqs.a: Punjabi first for Punjab, Hindi structure second for the nation. Each language halves the other's difficulty — learn one, get the second at a discount.

topics.lede: Cousin languages, sister scripts — shared words, split sounds.
topics.note: A note on ਘਰ = घर. Punjabi ਘਰ (house) and Hindi घर are the SAME word in sister scripts — thousands work this way. Learn Punjabi's core well and Hindi signboards start reading themselves.
paras: The cousins grew side by side: ਪੰਜਾਬੀ bloomed in Punjab, हिंदी spread across the north. Same Indo-Aryan mother, sister scripts — Gurmukhi rounded and open while Devanagari ruled with its headline. History in every sentence.

Shared words delight learners: ਘਰ/घर (house), ਪਾਣੀ/पानी (water), ਨਾਮ/नाम (name), ਦੋਸਤ/दोस्त (friend) — identical or near. Core vocabulary overlaps enormously; learn one list, own two languages' hearts.

Split sounds mark the border: Punjabi tones against Hindi flatness, ਮੈਨੂੰ (mainun — to-me) against मुझे, ਹਾਂ (haan — yes) against हाँ. Pronouns and yes-no drifted most — precisely the words learners say most. Drill the pairs; cross the border daily.

Greetings show both faces: ਸਤਿ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਅਕਾਲ stands Punjabi-proud while नमस्ते stands Hindi-classic — yet each understands the other's instantly. Cousins recognise cousins; learn either with love and both reward you.
topics.title: Punjabi vs Hindi

topics.desc: Dialogues, songs and bhangra beats — learn Punjabi the Pollywood way. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: Realistic dramas and comedies — clear speech, everyday words, repeatable ਡਾਇਲਾਗ (dialogues). Pollywood's realism teaches natural speech like no textbook.
Watch once with subtitles for story, again pausing to shadow dialogues, songs on loop for sounds. Three passes per film: story, speech, song.
faqs.q: How do I learn from films?

faqs.a: Start with famous lines — short, dramatic, unforgettable. Film dialogues stick like songs; mimicry is fluency's shortcut.

topics.lede: Dialogues, songs and bhangra beats — Punjabi the Pollywood way.
topics.note: A note on ਪਾਲੀਵੁੱਡ. ਪਾਲੀਵੁੱਡ (Pollywood) is Punjabi cinema's proud nickname — comedies that break records, dramas that win hearts, music that rules the globe. Bhangra beats teach rhythm; dialogues teach speech. Watch and belong.
paras: Cinema is Punjabi's second classroom: ਫ਼ਿਲਮ (film), ਥੀਏਟਰ (theatre), ਰਿਲੀਜ਼ (release) — Friday releases are festivals. ਅਦਾਕਾਰ (actors) and ਅਦਾਕਾਰਾ (actresses) are family members; ਨਿਰਦੇਸ਼ਕ (directors) are debated like philosophers. Watch and belong.

Genres teach registers: ਪਿਆਰ (romance) speaks softly, ਕਾਮੇਡੀ (comedy) snaps jokes, ਐਕਸ਼ਨ (action) barks orders. Romance first — gentle pace, tender words; comedy second — speed and slang; action last — glory without subtlety.

Dialogues drill memory: ਡਾਇਲਾਗ (dialogue) — repeat famous lines until they own you. Pollywood dialogues are realism with punch; delivering one correctly earns applause from auto drivers to executives. Shadow the stars shamelessly.

Music melts resistance: ਸੰਗੀਤ (music), ਗੀਤ (songs), ਭੰਗੜਾ (bhangra dance-songs) — learn lyrics line by line, sing them wrong then right. ਪ੍ਰਸ਼ੰਸਕ (fans) sing together; join them. Cinema Punjabi is joyful Punjabi — and joyful Punjabi sticks forever.
topics.title: Learning from Punjabi cinema

topics.desc: Friends, lovers, weddings — the Punjabi of hearts, spoken truly. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ਦੋਸਤ (male friend), ਸਹੇਲੀ (female friend) — then ਪਿਆਰ (love) and ਮੁਹੱਬਤ (affection) as bonds deepen. Friendship words first; romance follows naturally.
ਵਿਆਹ (spoken wedding), ਸ਼ਾਦੀ (grand wedding) — ਲਾੜਾ (groom), ਲਾੜੀ (bride). ਵਿਆਹ ਦੀਆਂ ਵਧਾਈਆਂ (wedding greetings) blesses every couple.
faqs.q: How do I talk about weddings?

faqs.a: ਮੁਆਫ਼ੀ (forgiveness) — ਮੈਨੂੰ ਮੁਆਫ਼ ਕਰੋ (please forgive me), then ਸ਼ਾਂਤੀ (peace). Punjabi reconciliations run deep and warm; ask sincerely, receive fully.

topics.lede: Friends, lovers, weddings — the Punjabi of hearts, spoken truly.
topics.note: A note on ਪਿਆਰ vs ਮੁਹੱਬਤ. ਪਿਆਰ (piyaar) is broad love — family, friends, humanity; ਮੁਹੱਬਤ (muhabbat) leans romantic. ਤੁਹਾਡੇ ਪਿਆਰ ਲਈ ਧੰਨਵਾਦ (thanks for your love) suits everyone; ਮੁਹੱਬਤ belongs to one. Punjabi loves precisely.
paras: Friendship opens hearts: ਦੋਸਤ (male friend), ਸਹੇਲੀ (female friend) — ਮੇਰਾ ਦੋਸਤ (my friend) introduces proudly. Punjabi friendships run lifelong and deep; ਦੋਸਤੀ (friendship) is celebrated in poetry, films and daily chai. Make one Punjabi friend and gain a hundred phrases.

Romance speaks softly: ਪ੍ਰੇਮੀ (boyfriend), ਪ੍ਰੇਮਿਕਾ (girlfriend), ਪਿਆਰ (love). Punjabi romance favours poetry over bluntness — Heer-Ranjha teaches the register better than textbooks. Learn gently; speak truly.

Weddings unite families: ਵਿਆਹ (wedding spoken), ਸ਼ਾਦੀ (wedding grand), ਲਾੜਾ (groom), ਲਾੜੀ (bride). Punjabi weddings run for days — bhangra, food, rituals, blessings. ਵਿਆਹ ਦੀਆਂ ਵਧਾਈਆਂ (wedding congratulations) is your ticket to the feast.

Bonds deepen and mend: ਪਿਆਰ (love), ਮੁਹੱਬਤ (affection), ਜ਼ਿੰਦਗੀ (life) — ਮੇਰੀ ਜ਼ਿੰਦਗੀ (my life) means my beloved. And when bonds strain: ਮੁਆਫ਼ੀ (forgiveness), ਸ਼ਾਂਤੀ (peace). Punjabi hearts forgive spaciously; ask with folded hands.
topics.title: Talking about relationships

topics.desc: Spaced repetition, topic decks, daily streaks — flashcards that actually work. Free, no sign-up.

faqs.a: ਫਿਰ ਫਿਰ (again and again) — but spaced: 1 day, 3 days, 7 days, 30 days. ਵਕਫ਼ਾ (spacing) beats cramming; ਯਾਦਦਾਸ਼ਤ (memory) loves intervals.
Five to ten per topic — quality over quantity. Master one ਕਾਰਡ deck fully before opening the next; half-known decks rot.
ਰੋਜ਼ (daily) short sessions — ten minutes, every day, no exceptions. Streaks compound; ਭੁੱਲਣਾ (forgetting) loses to routine.

topics.lede: Spaced repetition, topic decks, daily streaks — flashcards that work.
topics.note: A note on ਦੁਹਰਾਅ. ਦੁਹਰਾਅ (duhraa — revision, repeating) is Punjabi's own word for spaced review — recalling again, and again, at widening intervals. The language itself teaches the method: revisit, widen, remember.
paras: Cards carry memory: ਕਾਰਡ (card) — one word, one side; meaning, the other. ਯਾਦਦਾਸ਼ਤ (memory) strengthens with every recall; ਭੁੱਲਣਾ (forgetting) is just unreviewed memory. Build decks per topic — greetings, food, verbs — and review each separately.
Spacing schedules success: ਵਕਫ਼ਾ (interval) — review new cards tomorrow, then in three days, seven, thirty. ਫਿਰ ਫਿਰ (again and again), but wider each time. Cramming fills hours; spacing fills years.
Rhythms sustain streaks: ਰੋਜ਼ (daily) quick decks, ਹਫ਼ਤਾਵਾਰੀ (weekly) full reviews, ਮਹੀਨਾਵਾਰੀ (monthly) championships. Ten daily minutes beat Sunday marathons; streaks turn study into ਆਦਤ (habit).

Scores gamify growth: ਨੰਬਰ (marks), ਮੁਕਾਬਲਾ (contest), ਪ੍ਰਾਪਤੀ (achievement) — even ਹਾਰ (defeat) teaches. Quiz yourself, beat yesterday's score, celebrate loudly. Flashcards are games that pay in fluency.
topics.title: Flashcards by topic
